title: Ways of acquiring and losing citizenship
competency: List ways of acquiring citizenship, compare birth and descent, and explain voluntary and involuntary loss.

keywords.def: Citizenship by place of birth: born in a country, you become its citizen.
Citizenship by descent: your citizenship comes from your parents' nationality.
The legal process by which a foreigner applies and becomes a citizen.
Giving up your citizenship by your own free choice.
When the state takes away citizenship without the person's consent.

en.text: Each state makes its own rules about who its citizens are. The common ways to get citizenship are: by place of birth (right of soil), by descent from your parents (right of blood), and by naturalization. Naturalization is a legal process for foreigners, for example through marriage or adoption.

screens.title: Just move there?
screens.ask: Can anyone travel to any country at any time and become its citizen?
opts: No, they must meet that country's legal conditions
Yes, if they stay one week
screens.after: Each country sets its own legal conditions. Only people who meet them can become citizens.

screens.title: 1.2 Ways of acquiring and losing citizenship
paras: Citizenship is a legal status earned by being a registered member of a country.
Anyone can become a member if they meet the country's legal conditions.
International law leaves it to each state to define its citizens.
So different states have different rules for granting and losing citizenship.

children.label: 1. By place of birth
children.info: Right of soil: everyone born inside a state's borders becomes its citizen.

children.label: 2. By descent
children.info: Right of blood: citizenship comes from one or both parents, wherever the child is born.

children.label: 3. By naturalization
children.info: A foreigner applies and becomes a citizen through a legal process.

children.label: a) Marriage
children.info: A foreigner who marries a citizen may get citizenship on application.

children.label: b) Adoption
children.info: Legal parents adopt a child from another country and make the child a citizen.

screens.title: Adoption: common conditions
paras: The parents must be permanent citizens of the state, by birth or naturalization.
The child must be under the age of 18.
The child must be a permanent citizen of the state he or she is adopted from.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Citizenship by descent from your parents.
The legal process by which a foreigner applies and becomes a citizen.

screens.text: Citizenship by descent is also called the principle of…
screens.why: Descent means your parents' nationality decides yours: right of blood.

pairs: the principle of right of blood
citizenship from people recognised as legal parents
a foreigner who marries a national gets citizenship
screens.why: Each way has its own rule.

screens.text: What is the main difference between citizenship by birth and by naturalization?
opts: Birth is automatic; naturalization needs an application and a legal process
Naturalization is automatic; birth needs an application
screens.ans: Birth is automatic; naturalization needs an application and a legal process
screens.why: People born in the territory become citizens automatically. A foreigner must apply to be naturalized.

screens.text: Meron's parents are both citizens of country X. She was born in country Y. Under the right of blood, she is a citizen of…
opts: whichever country she chooses at birth
screens.why: Right of blood: wherever a child is born, citizenship comes from the parents' nationality.
screens.clue: Does right of blood care where she was born?

en.text: Citizenship can be lost, just as it can be gained. Loss of citizenship means a person is no longer a lawful citizen. It happens in two ways. Voluntary loss is when a person freely gives up citizenship. Involuntary loss is when the state takes it away, without consent, after a series of steps.

screens.title: Losing citizenship
screens.ask: How can a person lose citizenship?
opts: By giving it up freely, or by the state taking it away
screens.after: There are two ways: voluntary and involuntary. Read on.

screens.title: B) Ways of losing citizenship
paras: "Loss of citizenship" means a citizen is no longer recognised as a lawful citizen.
The process is different in each country.
People lose citizenship either voluntarily or by force, without their consent.

screens.title: Two kinds of loss
paras: 1. Voluntary loss: giving up one's citizenship by free decision. Most countries set requirements for this.
2. Involuntary loss: the state revokes citizenship if a person does not follow certain requirements.
Involuntary loss is not immediate. It goes through a series of steps.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Giving up your citizenship by your own free choice.
When the state takes away citizenship without the person's consent.

screens.text: Giving up your citizenship by your own free decision is called…

screens.title: Voluntary or involuntary?
items: The state revokes citizenship without consent
A person gives up citizenship to join another country
Citizenship taken away for not meeting requirements
screens.why: Voluntary: the person chooses. Involuntary: the state decides.

screens.text: Involuntary loss of citizenship happens immediately, without any steps.
screens.why: It must go through a series of steps.

screens.text: Why might a person voluntarily give up citizenship?
opts: To become a citizen of another country that does not allow two citizenships
screens.ans: To become a citizen of another country that does not allow two citizenships
screens.why: Voluntary loss is a free choice, often to take another country's citizenship. Being forced is involuntary.
screens.clue: Voluntary means the person chose it.

items.text: List the different ways of acquiring citizenship.
pool: By buying a passport at a shop
items.why: The book lists these three main ways.
items.clue: One option is not a legal way.

items.text: What is the main difference between acquiring citizenship by birth and by naturalization?
opts: Birth is automatic; naturalization is a legal process for foreigners
items.ans: Birth is automatic; naturalization is a legal process for foreigners
items.why: Born in the territory = automatic; naturalization = application.

items.text: How does someone become a citizen of a country?
opts: According to that country's rules: by birth, descent or naturalization
items.ans: According to that country's rules: by birth, descent or naturalization
items.why: Each state sets its own rules.
items.clue: Who decides who its citizens are?

test.text: Citizenship by place of birth is called…
test.why: Born on the land = right of soil.

test.text: All countries follow the same procedures in granting and loss of citizenship.
test.why: Each state defines its own rules.

test.text: A foreigner who marries a citizen and applies for citizenship gets it by…
test.why: Marriage is a form of naturalization.

test.text: When the state takes away a person's citizenship without consent, it is…
Which child can usually be adopted and made a citizen?
opts: A child under 18 who is a permanent citizen of the state he or she is adopted from
Only a child born in the same town
test.ans: A child under 18 who is a permanent citizen of the state he or she is adopted from
test.why: These are the book's common eligibility criteria.

notes.text: The book says citizenship by place of birth (right of soil) is "the most prevalent method". Worldwide, descent is more widespread, and Ethiopia does not use right of soil. The lesson does not repeat "most prevalent".
Naturalization sub-points are labelled "a) Marriage" then "B) Adoption" in the book; shown as a) and b).
Check-point questions about reasons for losing citizenship and people the student knows are open; one is used as the challenge, the others are left out.
